newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish Esem Spor sees $90 mln sales in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Turkish Esem Spor sees $90 mln sales in 1996.

text.p: Tight export markets for Turkey's leading sportswear producer Esem Spor will limit its increase in sales in 1996 to $90 million compared with $88.8 million in 1995, Osman Ayaz, president of the company said.

"We could not reach our export targets this year due to recession in main European markets like Germany and France and an overvalued Turkish lira. But we expect a $100 million turnover in 1997," he told a press conference.
Sales stood at $71.4 million in the first nine months, including $10.3 million of exports. Esem's major export market was Germany with $7.2 million, followed by the U.S. with $1.6 million.
Ayaz said the company's before-tax profits would reach 950 billion lira at the end 1996, after 646.6 billion in 1995.

Esem, owned 84 percent by industrial commercial and industrial Cankurtaran Group, currently holds 37 percent market share in the domestic sport shoes market and 47 percent in the sportswear market, said Ayaz.

With 600 outlets throughout Turkey, it produces under four universal trade marks -- Adidas, Slazenger, Le coq Sportif and Arena. Esem meets the bulk of its sales via local production and the rest through imports.

"We will concentrate on exports in 1997 with primary focus on shoe exports after finishing our (capacity expansion) investments," Ayaz said, adding that shoes currently had only 2.8 percent share in total exports.
The company targets a 4.2 million unit sale this year, including one million pairs of sports shoes, after 3.6 million total in 1995, including 795,226 pairs of shoes.
Ayaz said the company's shoe production would exceed 500,000 pairs at the end of the year and total output would be between 1,750,000-1,800,000 units.
Total production was 1.6 million units in the first nine months of 1996, including 424,054 pairs of shoes.
Adidas leads among the four trade marks with a 70 percent share in Esem's total sportswear and shoe sales in lira terms.
Ayaz said sales of Adidas brands were expected to total $58 million this year.
